name: Question 4
problem: Compute the arc length of $y=\frac{2}{3}{(1+{x}^{2})}^{3/2}$ for $x\in [0,3].$
worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\frac{2}{3}{(1+{x}^{2})}^{3/2},$ $a=0,$ and $b=3.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}{(1+{x}^{2})}^{1/2}\cdot 2x=2x\sqrt{(1+{x}^{2})}
$$

Now, let's compute $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}} & =\sqrt{1+{[2x\sqrt{(1+{x}^{2})}]}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}+4{x}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2{x}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =2{x}^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}=2{x}^{2}+1$ to the formula for the arc length, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+x)|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =[\frac{2}{3}(3)^{3}+(3)]-[\frac{2}{3}(0)^{3}+(0)] \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The arc length of a curve y=f(x) between x=a and x=b can be found using the formula L=∫ab1+[f′(x)]2dx.

In our case, f(x)=23(1+x2)3/2, a=0, and b=3.

First, we find the derivative of f(x): f′(x)=32⋅23(1+x2)1/2⋅2x=2x(1+x2)

Now, let's compute 1+[f′(x)]2: 1+[f′(x)]2=1+[2x(1+x2)]2=1+4x2+4x4=(2x2+1)2=2x2+1

Substituting 1+[f′(x)]2=2x2+1 to the formula for the arc length, we get L=∫031+[f′(x)]2dx=∫03(2x2+1)dx=(23x3+x)|03=[23(3)3+(3)]−[23(0)3+(0)]=21.
